statement: The log likelihood tends to minus infinity on escape from every compact subset of the positive shape quadrant.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} (hx : ∀ i, x i ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) (hne : ∃ i j, x i ≠ x j) : Tendsto (fun p : domain ↦ logLik x p) (cocompact domain) atBot

statement: Every nonconstant interior sample has exactly one positive shape pair maximizing its beta log likelihood.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} (hx : ∀ i, x i ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) (hne : ∃ i j, x i ≠ x j) : ∃! p, p ∈ domain ∧ IsMaxOn (logLik x) domain p

statement: Holding the first shape positive leaves a unique positive maximizer in the second shape, including for constant samples.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} (hx : ∀ i, x i ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) {h : ℝ} (hh : 0 < h) : ∃! b, b ∈ Ioi (0 : ℝ) ∧ IsMaxOn (fun z ↦ logLik x (h, z)) (Ioi 0) b

statement: Holding the second shape positive leaves a unique positive maximizer in the first shape, including for constant samples.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} (hx : ∀ i, x i ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) {h : ℝ} (hh : 0 < h) : ∃! a, a ∈ Ioi (0 : ℝ) ∧ IsMaxOn (fun z ↦ logLik x (z, h)) (Ioi 0) a

statement: A constant interior sample has no maximizing positive shape pair.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) {c : ℝ} (hc : c ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) : ¬ ∃ p ∈ domain, IsMaxOn (logLik (fun _ : Fin n ↦ c)) domain p

statement: A nonempty interior sample has a finite joint MLE exactly when two observations differ, and the MLE is unique whenever it exists.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} (hx : ∀ i, x i ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1) : (∃! p, p ∈ domain ∧ IsMaxOn (logLik x) domain p) ↔ ∃ i j, x i ≠ x j

statement: Positive shape pairs approaching the binomial face have the stated log-likelihood limit.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hx : ∀ i, x i ≤ m) {p : ℝ} (hp : 0 < p) (hp' : p < 1) : Tendsto (fun s : ℝ ↦ logLik m x (p / s) ((1 - p) / s)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (binomialLogLik m x p))

statement: If a value bounds every finite beta-binomial likelihood, it bounds the binomial trace for any interior success probability and data within the held trial count.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hx : ∀ i, x i ≤ m) {p b : ℝ} (hp : 0 < p) (hp' : p < 1) (hb : b ∈ upperBounds ((fun q : ℝ × ℝ ↦ logLik m x q.1 q.2) '' domain)) : binomialLogLik m x p ≤ b

statement: The empirical proportion maximizes the binomial log-likelihood over open probabilities.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hm : 0 < m) (hn : 0 < n) (hx : ∀ i, x i ≤ m) (hu : 0 < proportion m x) (hu' : proportion m x < 1) : IsMaxOn (binomialLogLik m x) (Ioo 0 1) (proportion m x)

statement: Overdispersion gives positive inverse concentration with likelihood above the binomial face.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hm : 0 < m) (hn : 0 < n) (hx : ∀ i, x i ≤ m) (hu : 0 < proportion m x) (hu' : proportion m x < 1) (hvar : (m : ℝ) * proportion m x * (1 - proportion m x) < variance x) : ∃ s > 0, binomialLogLik m x (proportion m x) < logLik m x (proportion m x / s) ((1 - proportion m x) / s)

statement: Underdispersion and exact equidispersion both give strict global binomial dominance.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hm : 2 ≤ m) (hn : 0 < n) (hx : ∀ i, x i ≤ m) (hu : 0 < proportion m x) (hu' : proportion m x < 1) (hV : variance x ≤ (m : ℝ) * proportion m x * (1 - proportion m x)) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) : logLik m x a b < binomialLogLik m x (proportion m x)

statement: The binomial likelihood is the unattained supremum in the nonpositive-dispersion regime.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hm : 2 ≤ m) (hn : 0 < n) (hx : ∀ i, x i ≤ m) (hu : 0 < proportion m x) (hu' : proportion m x < 1) (hV : variance x ≤ (m : ℝ) * proportion m x * (1 - proportion m x)) : sSup ((fun q : ℝ × ℝ ↦ logLik m x q.1 q.2) '' domain) = binomialLogLik m x (proportion m x)

statement: At fixed positive trial count, an interior count and a beta-binomial witness above the optimized binomial guarantee finite attainment.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hm : 0 < m) (hn : 0 < n) (hx : ∀ i, x i ≤ m) (hi : ∃ i, 0 < x i ∧ x i < m) (hu : 0 < proportion m x) (hu' : proportion m x < 1) {p s : ℝ} (hp : 0 < p) (hp' : p < 1) (hs : 0 < s) (hwin : binomialLogLik m x (proportion m x) < faceLogLik m x p s) : ∃ q ∈ domain, IsMaxOn (fun q : ℝ × ℝ ↦ logLik m x q.1 q.2) domain q

statement: With an interior count, strict overdispersion gives a finite global maximum.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hm : 2 ≤ m) (hn : 0 < n) (hx : ∀ i, x i ≤ m) (hi : ∃ i, 0 < x i ∧ x i < m) (hvar : (m : ℝ) * proportion m x * (1 - proportion m x) < variance x) : ∃ q ∈ domain, IsMaxOn (fun q : ℝ × ℝ ↦ logLik m x q.1 q.2) domain q

statement: For a sample with an interior observation, finite attainment is equivalent to overdispersion.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hm : 2 ≤ m) (hn : 0 < n) (hx : ∀ i, x i ≤ m) (hi : ∃ i, 0 < x i ∧ x i < m) : (∃ q ∈ domain, IsMaxOn (fun q : ℝ × ℝ ↦ logLik m x q.1 q.2) domain q) ↔ (m : ℝ) * proportion m x * (1 - proportion m x) < variance x
dossier_scope_note: Known trial count at least two, both shapes free, and at least one count strictly between the endpoints. No assertion about free trial count, endpoint-only histograms, or uniqueness.

statement: For counts at most the held size, the beta-binomial log likelihood is bounded above.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hx : ∀ i, x i ≤ m) : BddAbove ((fun q : ℝ × ℝ ↦ logLik m x q.1 q.2) '' domain)

statement: The best binomial value bounds the beta-binomial supremum from below.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hx : ∀ i, x i ≤ m) (hu : 0 < proportion m x) (hu' : proportion m x < 1) : binomialLogLik m x (proportion m x) ≤ sSup ((fun q : ℝ × ℝ ↦ logLik m x q.1 q.2) '' domain)

statement: An endpoint-only sample with a strict finite upper bound and a path to it has that unattained supremum.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hm : 0 < m) (hn : 0 < n) (h : (∀ i, x i = 0) ∨ (∀ i, x i = m)) : sSup ((fun q : ℝ × ℝ ↦ logLik m x q.1 q.2) '' domain) = 0 ∧ ∀ q ∈ domain, logLik m x q.1 q.2 < 0

statement: An all-zero sample has log-likelihood supremum zero, strictly above every finite value.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hm : 0 < m) (hn : 0 < n) (hx : ∀ i, x i = 0) : sSup ((fun q : ℝ × ℝ ↦ logLik m x q.1 q.2) '' domain) = 0 ∧ ∀ q ∈ domain, logLik m x q.1 q.2 < 0

statement: An all-size sample has log-likelihood supremum zero, strictly above every finite value.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hm : 0 < m) (hn : 0 < n) (hx : ∀ i, x i = m) : sSup ((fun q : ℝ × ℝ ↦ logLik m x q.1 q.2) '' domain) = 0 ∧ ∀ q ∈ domain, logLik m x q.1 q.2 < 0

statement: With first shape held positive and nonconstant log data, escaping log-affine coordinates lose likelihood.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] {D : Set X} {L : X → ℝ} (h : ∀ M, ∃ K : Set X, IsCompact K ∧ K ⊆ D ∧ ∀ p ∈ D, M ≤ L p → p ∈ K) : Tendsto (fun p : D ↦ L p) (cocompact D) atBot

statement: The fixed-first-shape likelihood tends to minus infinity on escape from compact subsets of its feasible parameter domain.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) {k : ℝ} (hk : 0 < k) {y : Fin n → ℝ} (hvar : ∃ i j, y i ≠ y j) : Tendsto (fun p : firstDomain ↦ firstLik y k p) (cocompact firstDomain) atBot

statement: At fixed first shape the two free coefficients have one finite maximizer.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) {k : ℝ} (hk : 0 < k) {y : Fin n → ℝ} (hvar : ∃ i j, y i ≠ y j) : ∃! p, p ∈ firstDomain ∧ IsMaxOn (firstLik y k) firstDomain p

statement: For constant log observations the path `b = -c * y₀` has unbounded likelihood.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) (k y₀ : ℝ) : ¬ BddAbove (firstLik (fun _ : Fin n ↦ y₀) k '' firstDomain)

statement: For each positive power the first shape has a unique maximizing value.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) (z : Fin n → ℝ) {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) : bestK z c ∈ Ioi (0 : ℝ) ∧ IsMaxOn (fun k ↦ scaleLik z (c, k)) (Ioi 0) (bestK z c) ∧ ∀ k ∈ Ioi (0 : ℝ), IsMaxOn (fun u ↦ scaleLik z (c, u)) (Ioi 0) k → k = bestK z c

statement: The profiled path converges to the normalized Pareto value, including ties at scale.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) {z : Fin n → ℝ} (hz : ∀ i, 0 ≤ z i) (hpos : ∃ i, 0 < z i) : Tendsto (scaleProfile z) atTop (𝓝 (paretoValue z))

statement: The finite two-shape likelihoods lie strictly below their Pareto supremum.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) {z : Fin n → ℝ} (hz : ∀ i, 0 ≤ z i) (hpos : ∃ i, 0 < z i) : IsLUB (scaleLik z '' shapeDomain) (paretoValue z) ∧ ∀ p ∈ shapeDomain, scaleLik z p < paretoValue z
dossier_scope_note: Scale held, all log ratios nonnegative and some strictly positive. The all-free Pareto comparison is a different result.

statement: With scale held, nonnegative log ratios and at least one positive log ratio, no finite pair of Burr shapes maximizes.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) {z : Fin n → ℝ} (hz : ∀ i, 0 ≤ z i) (hpos : ∃ i, 0 < z i) : ¬ ∃ p ∈ shapeDomain, IsMaxOn (scaleLik z) shapeDomain p

statement: With held scale, mixed log ratios below the scale on nonconstant data give a uniform tail loss for the profiled shape criterion.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) {z : Fin n → ℝ} (hvar : ∃ i j, z i ≠ z j) (hneg : ∃ i, z i < 0) : ∃ a > 0, ∀ c > 0, scaleProfile z c ≤ log c - 1 - log (1 / (2 * n)) - a * c

statement: The held-scale profile is coercive when the data vary and some lie below scale.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) {z : Fin n → ℝ} (hvar : ∃ i j, z i ≠ z j) (hneg : ∃ i, z i < 0) : Tendsto (fun c : Ioi (0 : ℝ) ↦ scaleProfile z c) (cocompact (Ioi (0 : ℝ))) atBot

statement: Nonconstant data with an observation below scale have a unique profile maximizer.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) {z : Fin n → ℝ} (hvar : ∃ i j, z i ≠ z j) (hneg : ∃ i, z i < 0) : ∃! c, c ∈ Ioi 0 ∧ IsMaxOn (scaleProfile z) (Ioi 0) c

statement: The maximizing profile point and its optimal first shape give the unique joint fit.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) {z : Fin n → ℝ} (hvar : ∃ i j, z i ≠ z j) (hneg : ∃ i, z i < 0) : ∃! p, p ∈ shapeDomain ∧ IsMaxOn (scaleLik z) shapeDomain p

statement: The held-scale constant sample at or below scale has unbounded likelihood.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) {z₀ : ℝ} (hz₀ : z₀ ≤ 0) : ¬ BddAbove (scaleLik (fun _ : Fin n ↦ z₀) '' shapeDomain)

statement: For positive power every real intercept comes from a unique positive scale.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {c s b : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (hs : 0 < s) : -(c * log s) = b ↔ s = exp (-b / c)

statement: The positive-rate likelihood has a real supremum, and every feasible point lies strictly below it, for a sample on an adjacent edge.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n c : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℕ) (hx : ∀ i, x i = c ∨ x i = c + 1) : IsLUB (logLik x '' domain) (sSup (logLik x '' domain)) ∧ ∀ p ∈ domain, logLik x p < sSup (logLik x '' domain)

statement: On all-zero data the full likelihood is maximized exactly at rate zero, with arbitrary feasible dispersion.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℕ) (hx : ∀ i, x i = 0) (p : ℝ × ℝ) (hp : p ∈ rateDomain) : IsMaxOn (fun q : ℝ × ℝ ↦ likelihood x q.1 q.2) rateDomain p ↔ p.1 = 0

statement: A nonzero sample on an adjacent edge has an unattained supremum even when the zero-rate atom is included. This includes every positive constant sample.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n c : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℕ) (hx : ∀ i, x i = c ∨ x i = c + 1) (hx0 : ∃ i, x i ≠ 0) : IsLUB ((fun p : ℝ × ℝ ↦ likelihood x p.1 p.2) '' rateDomain) (sSup ((fun p : ℝ × ℝ ↦ likelihood x p.1 p.2) '' rateDomain)) ∧ ¬ ∃ p ∈ rateDomain, IsMaxOn (fun q : ℝ × ℝ ↦ likelihood x q.1 q.2) rateDomain p

statement: At positive held scale, the entire argmax is a nonempty compact subset of the sample range. Maximizing over the sample range gives exactly that set.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) {s : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s) {i j : Fin n} (hi : ∀ k, x i ≤ x k) (hj : ∀ k, x k ≤ x j) : let A := {m | IsMaxOn (fun t ↦ logLik x t s) univ m} A.Nonempty ∧ IsCompact A ∧ A = {m ∈ Icc (x i) (x j) | IsMaxOn (fun t ↦ logLik x t s) (Icc (x i) (x j)) m}

statement: Every nonempty sample has a maximizing location at any held positive scale.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) {s : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s) : ∃ m, IsMaxOn (fun t ↦ logLik x t s) univ m

statement: At a tied location the density product factors into the scale power n minus twice multiplicity and the product over nonzero residuals.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (x : Fin n → ℝ) (a : ℝ) {s : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s) : logLik x a s = ((n : ℝ) - 2 * multiplicity x a) * log s - (n : ℝ) * log π - ∑ i ∈ off x a, log ((a - x i)^2 + s^2)

statement: The off-atom sum of log squared residuals is continuous as the scale tends to zero at the tied location.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (x : Fin n → ℝ) (a : ℝ) : Tendsto (fun s : ℝ ↦ ∑ i ∈ off x a, log ((a - x i)^2 + s^2)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (∑ i ∈ off x a, log ((a - x i)^2)))

statement: A strict-majority atom excludes a finite joint maximizer.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (x : Fin n → ℝ) {a : ℝ} (ha : n < 2 * multiplicity x a) : ¬ ∃ p ∈ domain, IsMaxOn (fun w ↦ logLik x w.1 w.2) domain p

statement: At half mass the collapse value bounds the log-likelihood. Equality holds precisely when the parameter pair lies on every semicircle through the atom and a distinct observed value.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (x : Fin n → ℝ) {a m s : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s) (ha : 2 * multiplicity x a = n) : logLik x m s ≤ collapseValue x a ∧ (logLik x m s = collapseValue x a ↔ ∀ i, x i ≠ a → (m - a) * (m - x i) + s^2 = 0)

statement: The half-mass collapse value is the joint supremum, attained exactly on the common semicircles through the half-mass atom and each other observation.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (x : Fin n → ℝ) {a : ℝ} (ha : 2 * multiplicity x a = n) : sSup ((fun p ↦ logLik x p.1 p.2) '' domain) = collapseValue x a ∧ ∀ p ∈ domain, IsMaxOn (fun w ↦ logLik x w.1 w.2) domain p ↔ ∀ i, x i ≠ a → (p.1 - a) * (p.1 - x i) + p.2^2 = 0

statement: A half-mass atom with two distinct other observed values gives no joint MLE.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (x : Fin n → ℝ) {a : ℝ} (ha : 2 * multiplicity x a = n) {i j : Fin n} (hi : x i ≠ a) (hj : x j ≠ a) (hij : x i ≠ x j) : ¬ ∃ p ∈ domain, IsMaxOn (fun w ↦ logLik x w.1 w.2) domain p

statement: At an unbalanced half-mass atom, every feasible path approaching the supremum collapses at that atom, with displacement negligible relative to scale.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {ι : Type*} {l : Filter ι} {p : ι → ℝ × ℝ} (x : Fin n → ℝ) {a : ℝ} (ha : 2 * multiplicity x a = n) {i j : Fin n} (hi : x i ≠ a) (hj : x j ≠ a) (hij : x i ≠ x j) (hp : ∀ᶠ z in l, p z ∈ domain) (hL : Tendsto (fun z ↦ logLik x (p z).1 (p z).2) l (𝓝 (collapseValue x a))) : Tendsto p l (𝓝 (a, 0)) ∧ Tendsto (fun z ↦ ((p z).1 - a) / (p z).2) l (𝓝 0)

statement: For a balanced two-point sample the entire joint argmax is the open upper semicircle with those endpoints.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) {a b : ℝ} (hab : a < b) (ha : 2 * multiplicity x a = n) (hx : ∀ i, x i = a ∨ x i = b) : {p ∈ domain | IsMaxOn (fun w ↦ logLik x w.1 w.2) domain p} = {p : ℝ × ℝ | a < p.1 ∧ p.1 < b ∧ 0 < p.2 ∧ p.2^2 = (p.1 - a) * (b - p.1)}

statement: If the held location has strictly less than half the sample mass, the scale is uniquely determined by the zero of its log-scale score.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) (m : ℝ) (hm : 2 * multiplicity x m < n) : (∃! s, 0 < s ∧ heldScore x m (log s) = 0) ∧ ∀ s > 0, IsMaxOn (logLik x m) (Ioi 0) s ↔ heldScore x m (log s) = 0

statement: If at least half the sample equals the held location, the log-likelihood strictly decreases with scale and no positive scale maximizes it.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) (m : ℝ) (hm : n ≤ 2 * multiplicity x m) : StrictAntiOn (logLik x m) (Ioi 0) ∧ ¬ ∃ s ∈ Ioi (0 : ℝ), IsMaxOn (logLik x m) (Ioi 0) s

statement: For a nonempty sample with all atom multiplicities strictly below half, a finite location-scale maximum exists.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) (hx : ∀ a, 2 * multiplicity x a < n) : ∃ p ∈ domain, IsMaxOn (fun w ↦ logLik x w.1 w.2) domain p

statement: The strict half-mass condition gives an attained, unique joint maximum.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) (hx : ∀ a, 2 * multiplicity x a < n) : ∃! p : ℝ × ℝ, p ∈ domain ∧ IsMaxOn (fun w ↦ logLik x w.1 w.2) domain p

statement: At two distinct equally frequent observations the admissible location-scale maximizer set contains the balanced midpoint and half-gap scale.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (x : Fin n → ℝ) {a b u : ℝ} (hab : a ≠ b) (ha : 2 * multiplicity x a = n) (hx : ∀ i, x i = a ∨ x i = b) (hu : 0 < u) (hu' : u < 1) : ∃ p ∈ domain, IsMaxOn (fun w ↦ logLik x w.1 w.2) domain p ∧ p.1 = a + u * (b - a)

statement: A joint MLE exists exactly under the strict half-mass condition or for a balanced two-point sample.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) : (∃ p ∈ domain, IsMaxOn (fun w ↦ logLik x w.1 w.2) domain p) ↔ (∀ a, 2 * multiplicity x a < n) ∨ ∃ a b, a ≠ b ∧ 2 * multiplicity x a = n ∧ ∀ i, x i = a ∨ x i = b

statement: A unique joint MLE exists exactly under the strict half-mass condition.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) : (∃! p : ℝ × ℝ, p ∈ domain ∧ IsMaxOn (fun w ↦ logLik x w.1 w.2) domain p) ↔ ∀ a, 2 * multiplicity x a < n

statement: For a balanced two-point sample, the held-scale argmax consists of the locations at the stated squared distance from the midpoint. This gives two locations below half the gap and one at or above half the gap.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) {a b s : ℝ} (hab : a < b) (ha : 2 * multiplicity x a = n) (hx : ∀ i, x i = a ∨ x i = b) (hs : 0 < s) : {m | IsMaxOn (fun t ↦ logLik x t s) univ m} = {m | (m - (a + b) / 2)^2 = max 0 (((b - a) / 2)^2 - s^2)}

statement: A unique scale MLE exists exactly when the held location has less than half the sample mass.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) (m : ℝ) : (∃! s, s ∈ Ioi (0 : ℝ) ∧ IsMaxOn (logLik x m) (Ioi 0) s) ↔ 2 * multiplicity x m < n

statement: If every real threshold is exceeded by some feasible objective value, the image is unbounded above.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {α : Type*} {D : Set α} {f : α → ℝ} (h : ∀ M : ℝ, ∃ p ∈ D, M < f p) : ¬ BddAbove (f '' D)

statement: Unboundedness above of an objective image supplies a feasible point beating any given real threshold.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {α : Type*} {D : Set α} {f : α → ℝ} (h : ¬ BddAbove (f '' D)) (M : ℝ) : ∃ p ∈ D, M < f p

statement: A feasible strict peak is the sole point satisfying global maximality on the domain.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {α : Type*} {D : Set α} {f : α → ℝ} {p q : α} (hp : p ∈ D) (h : ∀ t ∈ D, t ≠ p → f t < f p) : q ∈ D ∧ IsMaxOn f D q ↔ q = p

statement: A feasible strict peak gives unique existence and an unbounded objective rules out a maximizer.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {α : Type*} {D : Set α} {f : α → ℝ} {P : Prop} {p : α} (hyes : P → ∀ q, q ∈ D ∧ IsMaxOn f D q ↔ q = p) (hno : ¬ P → ¬ BddAbove (f '' D)) : (∃! q, q ∈ D ∧ IsMaxOn f D q) ↔ P

statement: An attained nuisance maximum on each fiber reduces joint maximization to the profiled problem.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {A B : Set ℝ} {L : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ} {a b : ℝ} (ha : a ∈ A) (hfirst : ∀ y ∈ B, ∀ x, x ∈ A ∧ IsMaxOn (fun t ↦ L t y) A x ↔ x = a) (hsecond : ∀ y, y ∈ B ∧ IsMaxOn (L a) B y ↔ y = b) (p : ℝ × ℝ) : p ∈ A ×ˢ B ∧ IsMaxOn (fun q : ℝ × ℝ ↦ L q.1 q.2) (A ×ˢ B) p ↔ p = (a, b)

statement: With positive standard deviation held, the unique mean maximizer is the sample mean.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) {σ : ℝ} (hσ : 0 < σ) (μ : ℝ) : IsMaxOn (fun t ↦ logLik x t σ) univ μ ↔ μ = mean x

statement: With mean held and a nonzero residual, the unique standard deviation is the residual RMS.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: (hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℝ} {μ : ℝ} (hx : ∃ i, x i ≠ μ) (σ : ℝ) : σ ∈ Ioi 0 ∧ IsMaxOn (logLik x μ) (Ioi 0) σ ↔ σ = sd x μ

statement: With mean held at every observation, the likelihood is unbounded.
